title: Kinematics inside mixed-topic questions
learning_outcomes: Isolate a Kinematics leaf inside a mixed-topic chain.
Carry earlier results forward with correct meaning, sign and units.
Use only supplied later-topic information while preserving whole-question context.
prior_knowledge_summary: Students can identify the assessed Kinematics model and choose words, graphs or equations.
Students can solve graph, constant-acceleration and ideal-projectile tasks.
new_learning: Separate Kinematics inputs and outputs from surrounding-topic calculations.
Preserve dependencies across a structured chain.
Recognise when later-topic information must be treated as supplied data.
not_yet_taught: Force, energy, deformation and electric-field formulas unless explicitly supplied.
Any later-topic explanation beyond the information in the prompt.
knowledge_boundary: Mixed contexts are used only to practise Kinematics leaves. Later-topic relationships are supplied where needed.

evidence_basis.canonical_audit: Read every mapped enrichment, whole canonical question JSON/text, official mark scheme and visually inspected each complete official diagram.

excluded_mapped_parts.9702_m23_22_q02_c: Force and tension are outside scope.

blocks.title: Where does Kinematics begin?
body: A spacecraft question mentions an electric field, a force and a particle that stops. You have not studied the field formula here. Can you still solve the motion step? Predict which information belongs inside a Kinematics box.

Yes. Initial velocity, final velocity, displacement and constant acceleration form a complete Kinematics step. The surrounding topic may supply one of those values, but it does not change the motion relationships.

figure.alt_text: A teaching sketch of context strip.

blocks.title: Draw a boundary around the motion step
body: Read the whole question so you know the story and dependencies. Then mark the Kinematics input, target and interval. Treat an earlier result as data, with its unit and sign.
Do not import a later-topic formula. If force, energy or electricity information is needed, the question must supply the needed motion quantity or the relationship.

figure.brief: Teacher sketch showing boundary box with simple arrows, boxes and short labels.
figure.alt_text: A teaching sketch of boundary box.

blocks.title: A particle brought to rest
body: A charged particle enters a region at 6.0 × 10^5 m s^-1 and stops uniformly over 0.018 m. The field context explains why it slows, but the Kinematics leaf asks only for acceleration.
Take forward as positive. Use v^2 = u^2 + 2as: 0 = (6.0 × 10^5)^2 + 2a(0.018). Thus a = -1.0 × 10^13 m s^-2. The sign says the acceleration opposes the motion.

figure.brief: Teacher sketch showing input-output chain with simple arrows, boxes and short labels.
figure.alt_text: A teaching sketch of input-output chain.

blocks.title: Carry answers forward without losing meaning
body: A mixed question is a chain. Write each result beside the quantity it represents, not just as a bare number. Keep extra figures until the end and carry the sign convention into the next part.
Formula to remember: v = u + at. Formula to remember: s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2. Formula to remember: v^2 = u^2 + 2as. Use the one whose variables match the isolated interval.

figure.brief: Teacher sketch showing worked electric-field handoff with simple arrows, boxes and short labels.
figure.alt_text: A teaching sketch of worked electric-field handoff.

blocks.title: Context does not choose the formula
body: It feels reasonable to use every formula associated with the story. That fails because a motor, spring or field can lead to many different targets. The target and available motion data choose the Kinematics relationship.
A distance-time graph after constant speed followed by slowing must first be linear, then curve with decreasing gradient until horizontal. The surrounding motor details do not alter that graph logic.

figure.brief: Teacher sketch showing misconception chain with simple arrows, boxes and short labels.
figure.alt_text: A teaching sketch of misconception chain.

blocks.title: Chain A: motion before force
body: A powered cart reaches 9.0 m s^-1 from rest in 3.0 s, then a later part asks about motor force.
Draw the Kinematics leaf around u = 0, v = 9.0 m s^-1 and t = 3.0 s. The target acceleration is a = (v-u)/t = +3.0 m s^-2.
Carry +3.0 m s^-2 with its sign and unit into the later force step. Motor power and mass are irrelevant to this Kinematics leaf unless the next part uses them.
Do not discard the story: it tells us the direction and that the same cart continues into the next step.

figure.purpose: Make the reasoning in chain a: motion before force visible.

figure.alt_text: Teacher sketch for chain a: motion before force.

blocks.title: Chain B: projectile before energy
body: A package leaves a platform horizontally at 12.0 m s^-1 and falls 5.0 m. A later part supplies its mass and asks about impact energy.
For the Kinematics leaf, mass is irrelevant. Vertical motion has u_y = 0, s_y = 5.0 m downward and a_y = 9.81 m s^-2 downward.
t = sqrt(2s_y/g) = 1.01 s, so horizontal displacement is (12.0)(1.01) = 12.1 m.
Carry t = 1.01 s and any required velocity components with units into the later part. Ignore the energy equation until the Kinematics result is secure.

blocks.title: Solve the leaf, then return to the chain
body: Use this routine: read the whole context, mark dependencies, isolate one interval, copy in earlier results with signs and units, choose the shortest valid representation, solve, and interpret the result in the story.
The new skill is not another equation. It is keeping the context while protecting the Kinematics model from unrelated detail.

concepts_taught: A mixed-topic question can be decomposed into linked leaves while retaining whole context.
A Kinematics leaf uses motion inputs that may come from an earlier part.
Later-topic formulas are not required unless supplied.
misconceptions_addressed: Every formula suggested by the context must be used.
An earlier numerical answer can be carried forward without its sign or unit.
A graph shape depends on decorative context rather than motion.
skills_students_can_now_use: Isolate a Kinematics step in a mixed chain.
Carry prior results with meaning, sign and units.
Solve the motion leaf and interpret it back in context.
next_lesson_can_assume: Students can choose an efficient Kinematics representation.
Students can isolate and solve Kinematics leaves in mixed contexts.
Students can audit dependencies, signs and units.
next_lesson_must_not_assume: Students have mastered every Kinematics demand under timed conditions.
Students can diagnose and correct all recurring errors without a checking routine.
